2027-01-20.title: Wednesday after the Second Sunday after Denho · Third Day of the Fast of the Ninevites · St Sebastian
readings: Jonah's prayer from the belly of the fish
2027-01-20.alt: Season of Denho. Moonnu Nombu, the fast of the Ninevites (Baooutho d'Ninwoye). St Sebastian, martyr. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-20.verse: saying, “I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me; out of the belly of Sheol I cried, and you heard my voice.
theo: On the third day we hear Jonah praying from the depths. Swallowed by the great fish, at the bottom of the sea, with weeds wrapped around his head, he does not despair: “I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me.” “As my life was ebbing away, I remembered the LORD; and my prayer came to you.” And on the third day the fish spews him onto dry land. The Fathers saw here Christ's descent into death and his rising, and also our Baptism: going down into the water and coming up to new life.

In the Gospel people tell Jesus of a disaster in Jerusalem, and he answers: do not think the victims were worse sinners than you; “unless you repent, you will all perish as they did.” Repentance is not for others; it is for me, now. Paul says: “you are all children of light and children of the day”; let us “keep awake and be sober.” Today the Church honours St Sebastian, the soldier who served Christ more than Caesar and twice faced death for him. Jonah prayed in the depths; Sebastian stood firm under the arrows. Both teach us that no depth is beyond God's hearing.
outline: Ask: when did you feel you were at the bottom of the sea?
“I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me.”
live: Tell God honestly about your deepest trouble.
Make your confession today or tomorrow.
2027-01-20.prayer: Lord our God, you heard Jonah from the belly of the fish and brought him up on the third day. Hear us in our distress, give us true repentance, and through the prayers of St Sebastian make us brave children of the light. Amen.
altar: Christ went down into the depths of death and rose; in the Holy Qurbono he lifts us up with him.

quick: Jonah prayed from the depths and God heard him.
Unless we repent we will perish.
We are children of light; stay awake and sober.
2027-01-20.action: Make your confession before the fast ends.
2027-01-20.question: Do I think repentance is for others, or for me?

family.explain: Inside the big fish, Jonah prayed to God, and God heard him! After three days the fish put Jonah on the land.
family.intention: We pray for those who feel lost and alone, and for soldiers and police, through St Sebastian.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we need to pray to God for help?”

illus: A fisherman from Alappuzha was lost at sea for two nights after his boat capsized, clinging to a plastic can. He says he prayed the words of Jonah he had heard in church during Moonnu Nombu. On the third morning a trawler found him. Each year now he keeps the fast in thanksgiving.

pm.open: Lord, you hear us even from the depths. Give us true repentance on this last day of the fast. Amen.
share: I called to the LORD out of my distress (Jonah 2:2). What distress can I bring to God?
Unless you repent (Luke 13:3). What do I still need to repent of?
You are all children of light (1 Thessalonians 5:5). Where do I live in darkness?
interc: For all who feel trapped in the depths.
For those lost at sea and their families.
For soldiers and police, through St Sebastian.
For true repentance in our Church.
pm.close: Father, you heard Jonah from the depths and raised your Son from the grave. Raise us to new life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we hear Jonah praying from the belly of the fish. At the bottom of the sea, with weeds around his head, he prays: I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me; out of the belly of Sheol I cried, and you heard my voice (Jonah 2:2).
There is no depth where God cannot hear us. On the third day the fish brought Jonah to dry land. The Fathers saw here the death and Resurrection of Christ, and our own Baptism.

In the Gospel Jesus says: unless you repent, you will all perish (Luke 13:3). We often think repentance is for others. Jesus says it is for me, now. Paul adds: you are all children of light and children of the day (1 Thessalonians 5:5).
Today we honour St Sebastian, who served Christ more than Caesar and did not fear death. On this last day of the fast, let us pray from our depths, repent honestly and stand firm. Amen.
kids: Children, Jonah prayed to God from inside a big fish, and God heard him! God hears us wherever we are.

intro: Theme: “I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me.”
The prayer from the depths, the call to repent, and the courage of St Sebastian.

sub: In the belly of the fish.
q: Out of the depths I cry to you, O LORD. Lord, hear my voice! Let your ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications!
Therefore we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
points.apply: Bring your deepest trouble to God in prayer tonight.

q: Cast away from you all the transgressions that you have committed against me, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit! Why will you die, O house of Israel?
No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all perish as they did.
points.apply: Make your confession before the fast ends.

q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
points.apply: Stand firm in your faith at work or school.

concl: No depth is beyond God's hearing.
Repent now, and live as children of the light.
2027-01-20.resolve: Make a good confession before the fast ends.
